newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Compensation coupons soar, BUX declines.
newsitem.headline: Compensation coupons soar, BUX declines.

text.p: The compensation coupons jumped to a new 52-week high on the Budapest Stock Exchange and stole the show an an easing share market, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 5,578.73 points, down 73.53. BUX futures ended lower for all maturities, by between 60.00 and 169.50 points.
Share prices moved, however, mostly lower, following trend on major European markets on what traders explained by the apparent end of an expansive period of the Budapest bourse.

"I think the market reached the end of an expansive period and investors will now review what to invest in," one trader said, adding that the dollar's weakening since the morning had little negative impact on prices.
The compensation coupons received more spotlight as they rallied to a new 52-week high of 805 forints as planned share-for-compensation coupon swaps triggered demand.
"Investors are buying coupons on preparations for swaps in Forte and Szabolcstej," one trader said earlier today.

Hungary's privatisation agency APV Rt announced a one-round public tender earlier this month for the management of the public offer in stakes in Forte Fotokemiai Rt photographic industrial and Szabolcs Tejipari Rt dairy industrial companies.
But the other trader said that investors were buying coupons on hopes that electricity supplier ELMU shares will be allocated to them.
The share market calmed down and another reason was that investors were waiting for the planned new phase of a selloff in oil company MOL shares, traders said. MOL fell 65 forints to end at 3,075.
Elsewhere on the market holding company Csopak rallied 20 percent or 500 forints to end at a new record high of 3,000 forints.
Meanwhile brewery Soproni Sorgyar also jumped to a record level of 5,700 forints. Soproni ended at 5,700, up 400.
